MoCA-Mask: click only vs. click + CMAS (text → click) — a failure case

Steering vectors from extra text guidance (“animal”, optimised text embedding + click minus the same click alone; five annotated training frames, site encoder.1 by leave-one-frame-out) added to click-only SAM3. One random positive click per frame, identical in all click arms. This is the one dataset where the reverse direction fails (paper Table S13): over the 16 test videos Dice@0.5 click only 0.659 → click + CMAS 0.592 (−0.067, not significant), text + click 0.634. The vector switches on large wrong regions (mean predicted area 32% of the frame vs. 1.1% for the ground truth); on MoCA the click alone is already as good as text + click, so there is little for the text to add. Videos shown: the largest loss, a moderate loss and the largest gain (selected by per-video Dice; masks are the paper's saved test outputs).

Frames and masks: MoCA-Mask (Cheng et al., CVPR 2022), derived from MoCA (Lamdouar et al., ACCV 2020); videos remain the property of their owners. Shown for research illustration.
